approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It breeds fresh offspring by rank-biased parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and one-to-three successive local mutations, applies its existing chemical and identity admission gates, and retains the best scored survivors. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted observations in the current session uses count fingerprints to predict each fresh pool. Correlated function draws choose the announced batch. After three consecutive non-improving batches, the same predictive means first restrict eligibility to the best forty pool members and then also help rank purchases inside that set; an improving batch restores unrestricted eligibility. The Parent has already removed an unexposed rejection-conditioned mutation-length floor.
approach.novelty: Separate the two uses of predictive mean during stalls by removing only its candidate-specific contribution to purchase values inside the existing eligible set. The original means still construct exactly the same top-forty mask, and the original correlated residuals still decide purchases. This tests whether fine preference within an already screened set contributes additional useful guidance. Same-Parent siblings instead removed ordinary mutation continuations or replaced the optimizer with regional local models or persistent tree search; none isolated this location consumer while preserving the original masked allocator.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-cf8d309c06de uses fitted location twice during restricted announcements, but its evidence does not isolate the value of the second, within-set use. All three actual summary.json/run.log pairs are complete: macro mean 0.607030316211131, population SD 0.030175277546149237 and seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439; the Parent reproduced its own Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d after removing an unexposed mutation floor. Read-only recounts of all fifteen Parent task logs and trajectories reproduce 88 restricted of 435 announcements, zero numerical fallbacks, and 4,350 accepted optimizer receipts. Keeping each recorded mask and residual while dropping location changes all 88 restricted purchase sets, displacing 413 selected identities across 13 exposed cells. The residual-only sets have lower summed original predictive mean in all 88 cases (349.0555213129648 versus 381.3589779841979 across the 880 purchases). These are actual-state choice forecasts, not unpurchased outcomes or continued alternative histories. The read-only aggregate is policy/scratch/r0056-03-improve-L01/parent-audit-summary.json; it cites every per-seed/task audit and underlying Parent log and trajectory explicitly, with their hashes recorded in policy/scratch/r0056-03-improve-L01/inputs-sha256.json. The mask-free full-location removal n-04741f9b1832 lost 0.182967629428378 against its own Parent and supports a positive location contribution only there. The mean-only removal n-c4c934fd6a68 lost 0.12689408391255833 while making the retained mask nonbinding, so it cannot answer this question either. The specific bottleneck is unresolved conditional usefulness of within-set location, rather than missing proposal support or demonstrated absence of all mean information.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen search-policy-r56-support-and-statistical-consumers review as an alternatives review, with its actual recorded queries. Adopt no external recipe. In this node the original GP fit and posterior mean remain intact, and only a successful restricted allocation consumer receives the constant archive location. RAVE blending, multivalid updates, coherent mean-basis GP conditioning and regional-model construction remain deferred or in other branches; none is claimed as this intervention.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The exact intervention is justified by Parent n-cf8d309c06de source and paid Search receipts: its means both restrict eligibility and set relative purchase location; the same-state residual-only replay changes all 88 restricted purchase sets and 413 selected identities while retaining the eligibility inputs. The published mask-free location control n-04741f9b1832 and mean-only control n-c4c934fd6a68 have different conditions and cannot isolate this consumer. The frozen review explicitly defers its external recipes, and this node introduces none of them. It makes a scoped internal contribution test with no new fitted model, dependency or asset.

hypothesis: Remove candidate-dependent predictive allocation location only when the inherited stall predicate requests the top-forty restriction and the original posterior allocation succeeds. Write R = original_score_scale * (original_normals @ original_pool_factor.T). On those restricted announcements active_sample_values = original_archive_score_mean + R; on every unrestricted announcement active_sample_values remains original_predictive_mean[None, :] + R exactly. The original GP mean remains active for constructing the identical top-forty mask. Original fitting, covariance, Cholesky jitter, residual scale, normal draw and consumption, availability updates and ascending-index first-maximum ties are retained. The causal claim is that removing this second mean consumer eliminates relative location within the eligible set and changes paid identities toward lower original predictive means; if the removed fine preference is useful beyond eligibility, full/late realized progress and the complete endpoint mean will fall. This is a partial-pathway contribution probe within m-000000000005, conditional on the mask and residual staying active, not removal of the fitted predictor or of all predictive-location influence.

finding_summary.headline: Within-set predictive mean adds useful guidance: removing it lowered the final score by 0.02309
finding_summary.insights: Mean-based eligibility does not exhaust the useful information in the fitted mean: its finer ordering inside an already screened set still adds value on this Parent. The surviving original GP predictions also had lower squared error than the constant allocation location on the same restricted purchases (0.01332 versus 0.02867), but these selected outcomes cannot establish calibration or rankings for unpurchased molecules. Removing that guidance produced broader scaffold coverage and lower similarity, including after small fragments were excluded, while yielding less total progress and fewer survivors and reused offspring. The method can reach varied molecular graphs; the evidence narrows the limitation to converting that variety into larger useful gains, rather than universal scaffold collapse. Late search still concentrates, and the Molecular assessment finds narrow high-scoring chemical families, tied peripheral analogues, reactive heteroatom-halogen motifs and missing specified stereochemistry. A proposal operator that distinguishes attachment environments, or a ranking/search model that better values useful structural changes, could address those limitations; neither was tested here. Chemistry is not an established mediator of this score loss. The result settles the conditional contribution of fine location guidance on this composition. It leaves the separate eligibility mask, total selector, alternative ranking models and transfer to other compositions unresolved; it does not end the broader approach.
finding_summary.results: The scoped removal executed in 93 of 435 batches and changed every restricted purchase set. It displaced 476 purchased molecules and changed 625 strict per-position choices; all reached accepted feedback. The original-mean eligibility mask, correlated residual and unrestricted rule were preserved. Summed original predictive mean fell from 367.52 for the same-state original choices to 328.83 for the actual purchases; 92 of 93 batches decreased, with one small increase. Across all fifteen matched Search sessions, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.583938, a paired change of -0.023092. All three seed averages fell; ten task/seed endpoints fell, two improved and three tied. Full and late incumbent-gain amounts fell from 5.97807 to 5.63169 and from 1.02241 to 0.85718. Improvement counts instead rose slightly, from 253 to 258 overall and 76 to 77 late, so the loss reflects smaller gains rather than fewer gains. Complete prediction joins and zero numerical fallbacks rule out a technical failure. The decrease crosses the registered 0.002 descriptive boundary for positive contribution of the retained within-set mean preference; it is not a performance improvement by the removal.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and amines retain reactive halogen bonds, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional fragment or size extremes
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-8e00e5e9fc34 against published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, restricted to frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten and 300 accepted observations per task/session. All fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectory files were read; no paths or paired task/seed comparisons were missing. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. Each cohort contains 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals after excluding the ten initial records per session. These trajectories do not describe every rejected or unpurchased pool molecule. Child digest ring-closure rates are 0.9713 to 0.9828 and aromatic-text rates 0.969 to 0.9747, consistent with abundant fused aromatics, heteroaromatics, saturated nitrogen rings, amides, lactams, ethers and halogenated substituents. RDKit perception of the accepted strings gives task median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 29, 31 and 27 in the frozen task order; 101 proposals have at most five heavy atoms, 44 exceed fifty, and 102 have no Murcko scaffold. The Parent has corresponding tails of 91 and 44 and 95 scaffold-free proposals. The late window, optimizer ordinals 146 through 290, still contains 36 Child and 33 Parent small fragments. Synthetic plausibility is mixed: conventional motifs coexist with N-halogen bonds in 1,066 Child versus 888 Parent proposals, O-halogen bonds in 169 versus 162, and peroxide bonds in 122 versus 118. These overlapping structural alerts are not measured instability or synthesis failures. There are 2,616 Child proposals with unassigned tetrahedral centres and no assigned centres; only one Child proposal has an explicit formal charge. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of basicity or biological protonation. Typed scaffold diversity is substantial, but high-score subsets are narrower; these are molecule-level associations, not attribution to an algorithm component, activation, or a recommendation to remove every alert. Provenance, original staging paths, Search scope and SHA-256 hashes are in policy/scratch/r0056-03-improve-L01-molecular/input-manifest.json; the reproducible descriptor definitions and comparisons are in policy/scratch/r0056-03-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json and the manifest-listed per-seed audits. Child input files are byte-identical run-relative snapshots of the exact frozen staging paths; Parent inputs are the existing published trajectories. No future archive path is assumed. All descriptor counts are derived from those trajectories using RDKit 2023.09.6; high-score deciles contain 87 pooled optimizer records per task ordered by existing recorded scores. Their scaffold counts describe those records and do not constitute new oracle scores. No synthesis, stability, protonation or three-dimensional geometry experiment was available, and no absent target-specific requirement can be deduced from the observed score gradient alone.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized fused azaaromatic or indole-like cores connected to another aromatic ring through a carbonyl or amide, with methyl/ethyl, methoxy and halogen decoration. The optimizer median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; its high-score decile spans 22 to 27 heavy atoms. The leading seed-1 amide has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, but carries an N-F bond. Seed 2 also reaches a fused azaaromatic aryl ketone with an N-N(F)C substituent. This is recognizable medicinal-chemistry connectivity mixed with unusual nitrogen-halogen chemistry. The Child has 236 typed and 74 generic scaffolds overall, narrowing to 16 and six in its high-score decile; the Parent narrows to 12 and five. Parent leaders remain in the same broad carbonyl-linked aromatic family.
liabilities: N-F and N-Br bonds on heterocyclic or exocyclic nitrogen make the stability and synthesis of many leaders questionable.
Twenty accepted proposals have at most five heavy atoms; ring-rich average output does not eliminate chemically impoverished excursions.
missing_features: The high-score family does not demonstrate comparably broad coverage of conventional nitrogen substituents: 82 of its 87 records contain an N-halogen bond. Stable alternatives preserving the observed compact carbonyl/aromatic arrangement remain underrepresented, rather than proven inaccessible.
A score-improving absent functional group cannot be identified from the tied local analogues; additional attachment patterns are a coverage question, not an inferred benchmark answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed maximum is 0.42956033293511225, whereas F and C=C score zero and the halogenated benzene Clc1ccc(Br)cc1 scores 2.2064040954992307e-13. Ring presence or halogenation alone therefore does not explain the higher scores. The better records combine a compact fused core with additional aromatic and carbonyl/amide environments. Several substitutions, including Br/F/Cl exchanges in the leading amide family, tie at 0.42956033293511225, so their individual benefit is unresolved. Parent seed maxima are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554 versus Child 0.40497388700123543, 0.42956033293511225 and 0.42956033293511225; these differing analogue paths do not identify a missing target group.

per_task.generated_character: Large, densely decorated heteroaromatic structures dominate: median 31 heavy atoms and four rings, with a broad size range reaching 96 heavy atoms. The seed-0 leader has a five-ring N-rich fused core, carbonyl and thione groups, a linked azaaromatic system, O-F substitution and a chloromethyl ether. Seed 1 explores multiaryl ethers with azaheterocycles, nitriles and S-Br substitution; seed 2 explores carbonyl-bearing aromatics with nitroso groups and contracted/fused ring closures. There are 351 typed and 248 generic scaffolds, but only 17 and eleven among the high-score decile. Parent and Child retain the same seed-0 and seed-2 leading molecules; the seed-1 leaders differ within a related azaaryl-ether family.
liabilities: Forty-two proposals carry O-halogen bonds, 241 have an N=O substructure, and 81 have peroxide bonds; these categories overlap and are chemistry alerts.

Eighty-five proposals, including 22 high-score-decile records, contain a perceived ring of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic. This flags unusual geometry without proving that every such structure is impossible.
There are 23 small fragments of at most five heavy atoms and 20 molecules above fifty heavy atoms, including unsupported size extremes.
missing_features: The leaders do not demonstrate stable, geometry-checked realizations of their dense heteroaromatic attachment patterns; synthetic routes and conformational feasibility are absent evidence.

Configuration-defined variants are missing even for the leading seed-0 molecule, which has two perceived but unassigned tetrahedral centres. The recorded scores cannot establish whether a specific configuration is preferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Tiny acyclic C#CC#C and BrSBr sit at the observed 0.5 floor, while the densely heterocyclic seed-0 leader reaches 0.8561477222467935. Seed 2 reaches 0.6442339647723496 with its nitroso-containing aromatic framework; these scores associate the stronger output with extended connected ring and heteroatom environments. They do not show that O-F, nitroso or S-Br bonds cause the gain. Parent seed-1 maximum is 0.6217289889933668 against Child 0.620364977674238; other seed maxima match. More ring content is not monotonically rewarded: the high-score decile has 28 to 43 heavy atoms and no greater-than-fifty-heavy-atom molecule.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output contains saturated cyclic and side-chain amines together with multiple halogenated aromatic rings, often phenolic or ether-linked. The optimizer median is 29 heavy atoms and four rings; the high-score decile is more compact, 24 to 33 heavy atoms with a median of three rings. The seed-1 leader combines a diaza saturated ring containing an aminal carbon, an aminomethyl substituent, two aromatic rings and a phenol. Seed 2 instead reaches an aminomethyl-bearing oxygen heterocycle with a tertiary alkylamine and a halogenated biaryl group. All 87 high-score-decile records match the explicitly defined non-amide aliphatic-amine SMARTS. Basic nitrogen chemistry is present, not missing. Parent leaders show related amine-rich families.
liabilities: The leading diaza ring contains an aminal environment; nearby high-scoring analogues also carry N-Br bonds. Their preparative and solution stability is unverified.
Small fused-ring motifs occur in other leading families, and heavy halogen decoration coexists with multiple basic centres. No measured physicochemical or selectivity profile is supplied.
Twenty-one proposals have at most five heavy atoms and 22 exceed fifty; none of the high-score-decile records lies in either tail.
missing_features: Specified stereochemistry is absent: every high-score-decile molecule contains an unassigned tetrahedral centre, and none contains an assigned centre. The geometrically defined versions of these amine-bearing frameworks were not compared.
Explicit ionic states are absent from this trajectory. Neutral depiction is not lack of ionisability, and the records do not establish a beneficial protonation-state intervention.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader scores 0.9999912943899532. In contrast, O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 scores 0.00016650955053713697: its ring nitrogen is sulfonylated, unlike the accessible aliphatic amines in the stronger family. That comparison supports an association with amine-bearing aromatic architectures, not an isolated causal test of basicity. Child seed-2 maximum is 0.9952488491767933 versus Parent 0.9735180254338864, with aminomethyl-bearing products prominent in the Child. These scores provide no independent measurement of affinity, protonation, selectivity or synthetic success.

per_task.generated_character: The generator explores carbonyl-rich saturated nitrogen rings attached to fused aromatic or azaaromatic systems, with ethers, N-methyl groups, imines and occasional N-N linkages. Median size is 31 heavy atoms with five perceived rings. The seed-1 leader couples a fused azaaromatic group to an O/N-containing ring and a carbonyl-bearing diaza ring; the seed-2 leader is a more bridged polycyclic arrangement linked through an O-CH2-N connection. This is the broadest typed-scaffold coverage in this Child: 591 typed and 399 generic scaffolds overall and 54 and thirty in the high-score decile, compared with Parent 559/379 overall and 42/22 in its high-score decile. Increased scaffold variety alone does not establish useful chemistry.
liabilities: Dense bridged and fused architectures complicate apparent synthesis; N-N and O-N connections appear among late products.
Sixty proposals meet the small all-aromatic-ring geometry alert, compared with eighteen Parent proposals; this is a structural difference, not a tested explanation for score change.
Fifteen accepted proposals have at most five heavy atoms and two exceed fifty.
missing_features: The search has many ring topologies but no stereochemically specified versions of the chiral aromatic/aliphatic hybrids: 86 of 87 high-score-decile molecules contain unassigned centres.

The records do not demonstrate a consistently higher-scoring, preparatively credible arrangement of the recurring azaaromatic, cyclic amine and carbonyl groups. The gap is useful arrangement and stereochemical resolution, not absence of those groups or wholesale scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed maximum 0.22656492228702677 belongs to the carbonyl-rich aromatic/aliphatic hybrid. C and C=C score zero, while the acyclic acetate CC(=O)OC(C)O scores 0.02244854133065254. More successful records retain several connected ring and heteroatom environments, rather than isolated small polar fragments. Child seed maxima are 0.21341170177721172, 0.22656492228702677 and 0.2261999694218064 against Parent 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313. Their mixed directions and varied frameworks do not isolate an absent required functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant productive family is a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyl and imino groups, linked to fluorinated unsaturated carbocycles and sometimes a saturated nitrogen ring. Median size is 27 heavy atoms and four rings; the high-score decile spans 23 to 30 heavy atoms. The best seed-0 molecule has an azetidine-like ring and a methoxy/chloro substituted nonaromatic diene ring, together with two N-F bonds on the fused core. The seed-1 leader instead retains a dicarbonyl core with an N-N(F)C substituent. Parent leaders remain in related fluorinated N-rich families. Child overall typed/generic scaffold counts are 324/136 versus Parent 274/101, narrowing to 34/17 versus 21/10 in their high-score deciles.
liabilities: N-F and O-F substituents, strained or unusually fused rings, and imino/enol-like heterocyclic environments make chemical stability and synthetic access questionable.
Twenty-two proposals have at most five heavy atoms; 22 also meet the small all-aromatic-ring alert. These are different overlapping counts, not a single failure category.
missing_features: Comparably successful stable alternatives to the N-F/O-F decorated core are incompletely represented: 64 of 87 high-score-decile records contain N-halogen bonds and seven contain O-halogen bonds. Carbon fluorination and ring amines already exist, so neither is an absent capability.

Specified configurations are missing from the fluorinated saturated centres: 77 high-score-decile records have unassigned tetrahedral centres and none has assigned centres. Their score benefit remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best Child score is 0.6545446155913083, while F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26 and FF scores 4.97400031457045e-24. A 45-heavy-atom peroxide-linked heterocyclic product scores 3.862281475007376e-18, so neither fluorine presence nor elaboration alone explains success. Compact fluorinated carbonyl/imino heterocycles carry the stronger observed scores. Parent maxima 0.7658605860985803 and 0.6443701453126088 exceed Child 0.6545446155913083 and 0.45847120515570783 in seeds 0 and 1; seed 2 ties at 0.6201223048692813 despite distinct leading substituent arrangements. The Parent therefore supplies stronger related examples, but not a demonstrated single missing chemical feature.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8e00e5e9fc34, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten, accepted optimizer observations only; comparison is published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. Among 4,350 Child proposals, 1,066 carry N-halogen bonds, 169 O-halogen bonds and 122 peroxide bonds, versus Parent 888, 162 and 118. Categories overlap. High-score families retain many of these environments. These are observed chemical alerts, not measured stability failures, and their association with high scores is not component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks reliable separation of conventional functional-group construction from reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide decoration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic chemistry capability would distinguish attachment-atom environments and offer conventional alternatives that preserve useful ring, donor/acceptor and linker relationships. Whether any restriction helps must be established from legal current-session feedback; these observations do not justify a blanket ban or a preselected intervention.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8e00e5e9fc34, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten, accepted optimizer observations only; comparison is published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. The Child has 2,616 proposals with 4,236 unassigned tetrahedral centres and zero assigned centres; its digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0 for every trajectory group. Only one proposal has explicit formal charge. Parent likewise has zero assigned centres and no explicit charges. Neutral amines are already abundant, so neutral strings are not evidence of missing basicity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic output is represented without specified configuration, and explicit ionic-state coverage is almost absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support preservation and differentiation of chemically valid stereochemical and ionic states within the identity contract, using only current-session observations to learn relevance. Missing representation coverage is established here; improvement from any particular configuration or charge state is not.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8e00e5e9fc34, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten, accepted optimizer observations only; comparison is published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. There are 172 Child and 170 Parent proposals containing a perceived ring of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic. Such alerts also occur in high-score subsets. The output contains numerous bridged and fused heterocycles; string parsing and accepted scores do not establish feasible geometry or a synthetic route.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring diversity includes unusual contractions and dense fusions without evidence that their three-dimensional geometry or synthesis is credible.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish graph validity from geometric and preparative plausibility when representing ring edits, and preserve access to alternative ring topologies. A geometry alert should retain its uncertainty; the present evidence does not authorize claiming all strained rings are impossible or assigning them an unmeasured score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8e00e5e9fc34, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten, accepted optimizer observations only; comparison is published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. The Child accepts 101 molecules with at most five heavy atoms, 44 above fifty, and 102 without a Murcko scaffold; Parent counts are 91, 44 and 95. The late optimizer window 146 through 290 still contains 36 Child small fragments. The higher-score deciles contain no molecules in either size tail. This is an accepted-stream association and does not describe rejected proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically useful scaffold retention is unreliable at both size extremes, even late in accepted search.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide ways to retain or reconstruct informative molecular environments during growth and deletion, and assess size changes against the current session rather than importing a fixed desired scaffold. Any size constraint would require its own evidence; these tails alone do not prove that a universal cutoff improves search.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8e00e5e9fc34, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, profile epoch 1, batch ten, accepted optimizer observations only; comparison is published Parent n-cf8d309c06de. Across the five frozen trajectory groups, Child overall typed scaffold counts are 236, 351, 322, 591 and 324, but the corresponding high-score-decile counts are 16, 17, 17, 54 and 34. Their generic counts are six, eleven, twelve, thirty and seventeen. The Child can produce distinct scaffolds; the observed limitation is concentration of successful chemistry and repeated tied peripheral analogues, not inability to make rings or universal collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad raw scaffold coverage does not consistently become broad coverage of plausible high-scoring chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to preserve access to chemically distinct attachment patterns and scaffold families while learning their utility from accepted feedback. Structural novelty is not itself improvement, and this report supplies no causal attribution or preferred intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
